why: The files and tools the briefs name exist: index.js, README.md, test/strutil.test.js, and `npm test` mapping to `node --test`. The Check 1 and 2 node commands and `npm test` look sound. Check 3 breaks. It is a double-quoted bash string containing `new RegExp('\\b' + f + '\\b')`. Inside double quotes, bash turns `\\` into a single `\`. So node gets the JavaScript `'\b'`, which is a backspace character, not a regex word boundary. No README heading contains a backspace, so every exported function would print MISSING whatever the README says. The syntax is still valid, but the command does not do what the brief says it does: a quoting mistake makes it wrong when run as written. It would need `\\\\b` or single quotes around the outer string.
